speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our assessment, how long has this lesion been present, and have you noticed any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. The history of an ant bite (likely a sandfly) preceding a chronic, enlarging ulcer on the leg in a patient with significant immunosuppression from Crohn's disease and prior steroid use is highly suggestive of this parasitic infection.
